key_insight: An unfitted hybrid high-order method can accurately simulate elastodynamic waves across an imperfect slipping interface without fitting the mesh to the interface.
engineering_relevance: This enables robust, high-order solid mechanics simulations for multi-material structures with unresolved internal interfaces, while remaining insensitive to cut-cell geometry and interface compliance.
method: Double the discrete unknowns in cut cells to represent both materials.
Use local strain reconstruction with a regularized interface stiffness matrix to enforce traction continuity and displacement slip.
Apply cell agglomeration to cure small cut cells and pair the semi-discrete scheme with Newmark or high-order SDIRK time integrators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2D numerical tests showing the predicted convergence rates for k=1,2,3 and robustness across sixteen orders of magnitude in interface compliance.
watch_item: The method relies on cut-cell agglomeration and interface regularization, so practical implementation may be nontrivial for highly complex geometries or very small cuts.
paper_title: An Unfitted Hybrid High-Order Method for the Elastodynamics Problem with Imperfect Interface
